title: Siman
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Bava Batra 113a has “Siman: Rabbah bar Rav Shila said.” Masoret HaShas suggests Siman may be a sage’s name.

Hyman considers it more likely that a mnemonic label is missing: אימ״ם, from the scriptural words ish, yidbakenu, matot and mimateh. Alternatively, he proposes the mnemonic בחב״ש, formed from the names of the Amoraim offering answers there. He cites the author of Dikdukei Soferim, note 9, for this view.

notes.text: אימ״ם and בחב״ש are proposed mnemonic labels. Neither is a new person called Imam nor a book called Chavash. Hyman’s two explanations concern the quoted verses or the responding Amoraim.

The consulted Bava Batra 113a contains the Siman phrase and the successive scriptural answers. The exact Masoret HaShas and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain Hyman’s reports; Siman is not thereby admitted as a sage.
